```{r setup}
library(inflascope)
cpi <- get_static_data("cpi")
hces <- get_static_data("hces")
```

## Introduction and research questions

What are observed all-India rural and urban price differences, and how do consumption weights affect modeled basket burden?

## Data sources and preparation

MoSPI CPI base 2024=100, published rate observations and HCES 2023–24 non-imputed MPCE (see README).

## Rural–urban inflation trends

```{r}
print(cpi[,c("date","sector","inflation_yoy","index")])
print(compare_rural_urban(data=cpi))
```

## Household consumption differences

```{r}
print(hces)
```

## Scenario experiment (hypothetical)

```{r}
print(inflation_burden(c(Food=8,`Non-food`=4)))
print(simulate_budget(25000,c(Food=.47,`Non-food`=.53),c(Food=8,`Non-food`=4)))
```

## Forecasting methodology and evaluation

The bundled reference dates are discontinuous. Forecasts and MAE/RMSE are intentionally withheld until sufficiently long, compatible monthly data are imported.

## Limitations and conclusions

Modelled constant-quantity basket costs are not empirical behavioural changes or causal effects. No 2012-base to 2024-base concatenation is performed. Stronger inferences require harmonized time-series data and household microdata.
